justification: The most specific correspondence is the flat, shallow-relief quadruped seen in strict profile with stubby splayed legs and an outstretched body, which appears at the right of A and again among the figures on B's pillar, carved in the same coarse tan stone. The biggest difference is organisation and relief depth: A is dominated by a single almost fully three-dimensional sculpted creature crouching on a block edge, whereas B is a flat upright slab covered in stacked registers of low-relief motifs (arched band, striped band, discs, birds) with no comparable ordering in A.
